title: Education Benefits Schedule of Benefit Levels and Tuition and Fees Terms by Chapter
content:
**Schedule A — Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education): qualifying basis, benefit level and tuition and fees terms, academic year August 1, 2025 through July 31, 2026.**

Each education benefit record is held under one official tier. The tier fixes the benefit level (the percentage the Post-9/11 GI Bill applies to tuition and fees, housing and books) and whether, and on what terms, tuition and fees are paid directly to the school. The chapters paid at a flat monthly rate carry a benefit level of 0 percent, because nothing they pay is scaled by a benefit level.

### A.1 Qualifying basis of each tier

| Tier | Qualifying basis |
|---|---|
| Montgomery GI Bill - Selected Reserve (Chapter 1606) | A six-year Selected Reserve obligation and a high school diploma |
| Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (Chapter 35) | A sponsor whose disability is permanent and total, or who died of a service-connected cause |
| Montgomery GI Bill - Active Duty (Chapter 30) | At least 36 months of active duty, the $1200 basic pay reduction paid, and an honorable discharge |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 60% Benefit Level | Aggregate active service after September 10, 2001 of 6 to less than 18 months |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 70% Benefit Level | 18 to less than 24 months |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 80% Benefit Level | 24 to less than 30 months |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 90% Benefit Level | 30 to less than 36 months |
| Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 100% Benefit Level | 36 months or more, or a Purple Heart, or 30 continuous days of service ended by a service-connected disability discharge |

### A.2 Benefit level and tuition and fees terms

| Tier | Benefit level | Tuition and fees paid directly to the school | Annual cap at a private or foreign school (before the benefit level) | Net in-state tuition and fees at a public school paid with no dollar cap (before the benefit level) | Yellow Ribbon matching available | Yellow Ribbon paid only under a school agreement covering the program | Tuition paid once per certified term |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Chapter 1606 | 0 percent | No | $0.00 | No | No | Yes | No |
| Chapter 35 | 0 percent | No | $0.00 | No | No | Yes | No |
| Chapter 30 | 0 percent | No | $0.00 | No | No | Yes | No |
| Chapter 33, 60% Benefit Level | 60 percent | Yes | $29920.95 | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| Chapter 33, 70% Benefit Level | 70 percent | Yes | $29920.95 | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| Chapter 33, 80% Benefit Level | 80 percent | Yes | $29920.95 | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| Chapter 33, 90% Benefit Level | 90 percent | Yes | $29920.95 | Yes | No | Yes | Yes |
| Chapter 33, 100% Benefit Level | 100 percent | Yes | $29920.95 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

### A.3 Reading the schedule

- The $29920.95 figure is the most that is payable for tuition and fees in one academic year at a private or foreign school, measured before the benefit level is applied.
- Only the Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) - 100% Benefit Level can receive Yellow Ribbon matching, and on every tier Yellow Ribbon is paid only where the school has an agreement covering the student's program.
- Chapter 30, Chapter 35 and Chapter 1606 pay the school nothing directly; the Chapter 33 levels pay the school once for each certified term rather than month by month.

*Hypothetical reading:* a student on the 80% Benefit Level at a private school is measured against the $29920.95 annual cap and the 80 percent level; a student on Chapter 35 at the same school has no tuition and fees line in this schedule at all.
